newsitem.title: UK: Shell says three more staff hurt in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Shell says three more staff hurt in Nigeria.

text.p: Oil giant Shell said on Tuesday three more workers were hurt, one seriously, in an incident at an oil pumping station in Nigeria occupied at the weekend by villagers involved in a local political
Shell said more than 120 of its staff and contractors were still being held by the villagers who overran six oil flow stations in the western Niger Delta on Saturday.
"We regret to report that three more of the detainees were injured in a further incident last night...One is thought to be seriously hurt," said Shell spokesman Julian Barnes.

Shell said the community groups holding the staff and contractors in protest at the relocation of a local government headquarters had agreed to release all the injured staff but the company could not say when that would happen. Some of the six workers hurt in Saturday's raid on the stations, which forced Shell to cut back oil production by 100,000 barrels per day (bpd), were released late on Monday, the spokesman said.
Shell said it was still losing 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Nigerian crude oil production after Niger Delta villagers occupied six flow stations on Saturday.
But exports and other supply commitments continued to be met, a Shell spokesman in London said.
Nigeria, a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), produces 2.15 million barrels per day of crude of which Shell accounts for half.
The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Group's Shell said it planned a peaceful resolution to the feud between two villages in the oil-rich Delta.
